title: Share Trading Policy

tiers.name: co-workers
tiers.description: Amcor employees generally. Bound by the Blackout Periods, the short selling, hedging and short-term trading prohibitions and the margin lending / secured financing consent requirement, but not by the pre-trade notification and confirmation regime in clause 10, which names only Directors and Executive Team Members and their Associates.

tiers.name: Executive Team Members
tiers.description: A member of the Corporate Executive Team, a member of the Global Management Team, key management personnel as defined in AASB 124, or a person designated as such by the Company Secretary and Executive Vice President Human Resources. Subject to the pre-trade notification to the CEO, the express Blackout Period ban on Derivatives, swaps, caps and collars, the minimum shareholding confirmation and annual certification.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: A non-executive director or an executive director of Amcor Limited. Subject to pre-trade notification to the Chairman of the Board (the Chairman notifies the Chairman of the Audit & Compliance Committee), ASX notifiable interest reporting within 2 business days, and annual certification.

tiers.name: Associates of Executive Team Members
tiers.description: A person the Executive Team Member is acting in concert with, or over whom the Executive Team Member has or can be regarded as having investment control or influence: spouses or partners including de factos, family members including children, nominees including investment managers, trusts of which the person, a family member or a family controlled company is trustee or beneficiary, partners, and controlled companies. The Executive Team Member must seek approvals and give notifications on the Associate's behalf.

tiers.name: Associates of Directors
tiers.description: Same definition of Associate applied to Directors. Bound by the Blackout Periods, short selling and hedging prohibitions, and may not trade until the Director has given the clause 10 notification and confirmation has been received.

definitions.hedging_definition: hedging arrangements (including, for example, the use of put and call options or other derivative instruments)

windows.start_anchor: close of trading on 31 December each year
windows.end_anchor: the day of the announcement to the ASX of Amcor's half year results (usually in the third week of February)

windows.start_anchor: close of trading on 30 June each year
windows.end_anchor: the day of the announcement of Amcor's full year results (usually in the third week of August)

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may specify 'any other period' as a Blackout Period from time to time; if it does, communications will be sent to those affected, so ad hoc blackouts are notified rather than confidential.

rules.detail: Derivatives, and financial products issued or created over or in respect of Amcor Securities, are expressly named for Executive Team Members and expressly instanced as swaps, caps and collars. They are banned outright in a Blackout Period. Outside a Blackout Period they are permitted but subject to the clause 10 notification, which requires confirmation from the CEO (copied to the Company Secretary) before trading. Derivatives are defined to include over the counter options, so venue is immaterial.
rules.evidence: If you are an Executive Team Member, you are prohibited from Trading in a Blackout Period in Derivatives, financial products issued or created over or in respect of Amcor Securities. Examples of these financial products include swaps, caps and collars.

rules.detail: The express Blackout Period ban in 9(a) names only Executive Team Members, but Derivatives are Securities and Directors are prohibited from Trading in Amcor Securities in a Blackout Period under clause 8, so the outcome is the same. Outside a Blackout Period, clause 9(b) subjects Derivatives trading to the notification procedures, meaning notification to the Chairman of the Board (Chairman of the Audit & Compliance Committee for the Chairman) with a copy to the Company Secretary and confirmation received before trading.
rules.evidence: Trading in Derivatives outside a Blackout Period is subject to the notification procedures in this policy.

rules.detail: Co-workers are not listed in the clause 10 notification table, so the notification procedures referred to in 9(b) do not reach them. Derivatives are Securities, so co-workers may not trade them in a Blackout Period or while holding price sensitive information, but outside those constraints no clearance is required.
rules.evidence: “Securities” means shares and other instruments considered to be a security for the purposes of the Corporations Act. The definition of a Security is complex and includes not only ordinary shares but also Derivatives, and any other financial products that are able to be traded on a financial market.

rules.detail: Absolute ban, extended to Associates, on hedging arrangements over unvested Securities issued under any employee or director option or share plan. Put and call options are expressly named as examples, so a collar over unvested plan securities is squarely prohibited with no consent route.
rules.evidence: You and your Associates must not engage in hedging arrangements (including, for example, the use of put and call options or other derivative instruments) over unvested Securities issued pursuant to any employee or director option or share plan.

rules.detail: Hedging over vested Securities is expressly contemplated and permitted, but must comply with this Policy (Blackout Periods, notification and confirmation, short-term trading ban, insider trading law) and, where applicable, with Amcor's Minimum Shareholding Policy. The clause 10 notification must confirm the Executive Team Member will be in compliance with the minimum shareholding policy after the trade, so a collar that takes the effective holding below the minimum is the binding constraint on size.
rules.evidence: In addition, any hedging over vested Securities must comply with this Policy and if applicable to you, Amcor’s Minimum Shareholding Policy.

rules.detail: Hedging over vested Securities is permitted provided it complies with the Policy, which for a Director means outside a Blackout Period, after notification to the Chairman of the Board (copied to the Company Secretary) and receipt of confirmation, no inside information, and no short-term trading. The Minimum Shareholding Policy applies only 'if applicable to you'; the express minimum shareholding confirmation in clause 10(a)(i) is drafted for Executive Team Members.
rules.evidence: In addition, any hedging over vested Securities must comply with this Policy and if applicable to you, Amcor’s Minimum Shareholding Policy.

rules.detail: The policy draws the line at vesting rather than at release from plan restrictions, but Appendix 1 item 6 makes clear that plan securities remain governed by the plan until they cease to be held under its terms. Securities that have not vested, including those still subject to plan holding conditions before vesting, cannot be hedged; the policy does not separately address shares that have vested but remain locked under a holding lock.
rules.evidence: Amcor Securities issued under an employee share plan provided that where securities granted under that plan cease to be held under the terms of the plan, any subsequent Trading of those Securities must be in accordance with the Amcor Share Trading Policy;

rules.detail: Monetisation, prepaid forwards and similar structures are not named. A structure that transfers the beneficial or legal interest in Amcor Securities is Trading, and a cash-settled structure over Amcor Securities is a Derivative or a financial product created over Amcor Securities, so either way it requires the clause 10 notification and confirmation for Directors and Executive Team Members and is barred in Blackout Periods. If the structure is secured on Amcor Securities it additionally needs the Company Secretary's prior consent under clause 17.
rules.evidence: “Trade” and “Trading” includes subscribing for, buying, selling or otherwise transferring the beneficial or legal interest in Securities of Amcor.

rules.detail: Outright ban on short selling for all persons covered and their Associates, defined narrowly as borrow-and-sell. A covered written call or a put purchased against shares actually held is not a borrow-and-sell and so is outside this definition, but a naked short position would be caught.
rules.evidence: You and your Associates must not engage in short selling. Short selling refers to the technique where a person borrows the security for the purpose of selling it in the hope that they will be able to buy the security back for a lower price at a point in the future and close out their position at a profit.

rules.detail: Securities lending as a lender is not named and is not within the definition of Trade, which turns on subscribing, buying, selling or transferring the beneficial or legal interest. Borrowing securities is mentioned only as an element of the short selling definition.

Contracts for differences are expressly inside the definition of Derivatives, so they follow the derivatives regime: banned for Executive Team Members in a Blackout Period, and subject to the clause 10 notification and confirmation outside it for Directors and Executive Team Members. A CFD closed within three months would also breach the short-term trading ban.
rules.evidence: “Derivatives” includes warrants, exchange traded and over the counter options and contracts for differences.

rules.detail: Margin lending over Amcor Securities is not banned. It is permitted for all covered persons and their Associates with the prior consent of the Company Secretary. No criteria, form, timing or conditions for that consent are stated, and no tier is excluded.
rules.evidence: You and your Associates are not permitted to enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Amcor Securities without the prior consent of the Company Secretary.

rules.detail: Granting security over Amcor Securities as part of a margin loan or other secured financing arrangement requires the Company Secretary's prior consent. A charge, lien or pledge unconnected with a financing is not named, and the definition of Trade does not expressly capture the grant of security, although an outright transfer of the legal interest to a security trustee would be Trading.
rules.evidence: You and your Associates are not permitted to enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Amcor Securities without the prior consent of the Company Secretary.

rules.detail: The clause reaches beyond margin loans to 'other secured financing arrangements in respect of Amcor Securities', which captures the loan leg of a funded collar secured on the collared shares. It is a consent regime, not a prohibition, and the sole gatekeeper is the Company Secretary. The policy is silent on whether consent may be conditioned, how long it lasts and whether it can be withdrawn.
rules.evidence: You and your Associates are not permitted to enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Amcor Securities without the prior consent of the Company Secretary.

rules.detail: The secured financing consent requirement is not limited by security state and there is no express ban on pledging unvested plan securities. In practice unvested plan securities are typically not transferable and any economic protection over them would be a prohibited hedge under clause 16, so the useful collateral is vested shares.
rules.evidence: You and your Associates must not engage in hedging arrangements (including, for example, the use of put and call options or other derivative instruments) over unvested Securities issued pursuant to any employee or director option or share plan.

rules.detail: A buy-sell window test rather than an intention test: trading in and out of Securities within a consecutive three month period is prohibited. Because Securities include Derivatives, an option position opened and closed inside three months is caught, so a collar and any unwind, roll or early termination must be spaced more than three months apart. No carve-outs are stated.
rules.evidence: Short-term Trading is prohibited under this policy. Short-term Trading refers to Trading in and out of Securities within a consecutive three month period.

clearance.post_trade_to: Chairman and the ASX, via the Company Secretary, of any change to notifiable interests; and annual certification of compliance to the Company Secretary
clearance.post_trade_deadline: no later than two (2) business days from the date the change occurred (Amcor must then notify ASX within five business days); certification following the end of each financial year
clearance.evidence: DIRECTORS, DIRECTORS’ ASSOCIATES, EXECUTIVE TEAM MEMBERS OR THEIR ASSOCIATES MUST NOT TRADE IN AMCOR’S SECURITIES UNTIL THIS NOTIFICATION HAS TAKEN PLACE AND CONFIRMATION HAS BEEN RECEIVED THAT THE TRADE CAN PROCEED. ... specify the proposed dates of the trade which should be no more than two weeks

BEFORE any Trading in Amcor’s Securities by: Executive Team Members; Directors; Associates of Executive Team Members; and Associates of Directors, the following notification for their intended Trade or their Associate’s intended Trade must be made

exceptions.approver: Company Secretary for co-workers; Chief Executive Officer or the Chairman of the Board for Directors and Executive Team Members
exceptions.evidence: It is recognised that exceptional circumstances specific to individuals may require a person to dispose of Amcor Securities during a Blackout Period. ... you will be in severe financial hardship if you cannot Trade in the Amcor Securities. Financial hardship would mean you were unable to meet your reasonable and immediate living expenses;

exceptions.approver: Chief Executive Officer or the Chairman of the Board
exceptions.evidence: you or your Associate are required by a court order to transfer or sell the Amcor securities;

exceptions.approver: Chairman of the Board or, where the Chairman of the Board is involved, the Chairman of the Audit & Compliance Committee
exceptions.evidence: the circumstance has been deemed exceptional by the Chairman of the Board or, where the Chairman of the Board is involved, the Chairman of the Audit & Compliance Committee.
an involuntary disposal of Amcor Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights;

transfers of Amcor Securities already held by co-workers, Directors or their Associates into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the co-worker, Director or their Associate is a beneficiary;

where the co-worker, Director or Associate is a trustee, trading in Amcor Securities by that trust provided that the co-worker, Director or Associate is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a Blackout Period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independent of the co-worker, Director or Associate;
trading in Amcor Securities in a managed securities portfolio where the co-worker, Director or their Associates are not in a position to influence the portfolio investments;

trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the Amcor Security holders, such as, a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Amcor Board.

Amcor Securities issued under an employee share plan provided that where securities granted under that plan cease to be held under the terms of the plan, any subsequent Trading of those Securities must be in accordance with the Amcor Share Trading Policy;
the acquisition of Amcor Securities by a Director to satisfy a share qualification.

exceptions.evidence: If a tax liability arises immediately upon awards which vest during a Blackout Period, the co-worker may sell or transfer the awards received in the period of 4 weeks immediately after the awards have vested in order to meet the tax liability.

Directors and Executive Team Members; annually following the end of each financial year; to the Company Secretary; certification that they and their Associates are in compliance with this policy or advice of any breaches

Directors; on any change to notifiable interests in Amcor Securities, which includes indirect holdings; to the Chairman and the ASX via the Company Secretary; no later than two business days from the date the change occurred
financing.minimum_shareholding_requirement: Amcor's Minimum Shareholding Policy is referenced but not reproduced. Hedging over vested Securities must comply with it 'if applicable to you', and an Executive Team Member's pre-trade notification must confirm they will be in compliance with the minimum shareholding policy after the trade. The policy does not say whether shares subject to a hedge or pledged as collateral still count towards the minimum.

external_documents: Amcor employee and director option and share plan rules, including the Long Term Incentive Plan
exemption_authority: Company Secretary consents to margin lending and other secured financing arrangements (clause 17) and approves exceptional-circumstances trading by co-workers in a Blackout Period; the Chief Executive Officer or the Chairman of the Board approves exceptional-circumstances trading by Directors and Executive Team Members; the Chairman of the Board (or the Chairman of the Audit & Compliance Committee where the Chairman is involved) may deem a circumstance exceptional; the Board may designate exceptions to the Blackout Periods, as it has for US tax liabilities on LTI vesting. Any clearance may be given or refused in Amcor's sole discretion without reasons.

bespoke_clauses.topic: secured financing is consent-based, not banned
bespoke_clauses.clause: You and your Associates are not permitted to enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Amcor Securities without the prior consent of the Company Secretary.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is available to Directors, Executive Team Members and co-workers on a single consent from the Company Secretary, making Amcor one of the policies under which the structure is achievable.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If you are an Executive Team Member, you are prohibited from Trading in a Blackout Period in Derivatives, financial products issued or created over or in respect of Amcor Securities. Examples of these financial products include swaps, caps and collars.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Collars are named and are prohibited only during Blackout Periods, which confirms by implication that a collar entered outside a Blackout Period with the required notification is contemplated by the policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Amcor Share Trading Policy does not apply to ... an involuntary disposal of Amcor Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank enforcing its security or a margin call sale during a Blackout Period falls outside the policy entirely, so the lender's enforcement rights do not put the executive in breach - a materially better position than policies that treat forced sales as a breach.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short-term Trading refers to Trading in and out of Securities within a consecutive three month period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because Securities include Derivatives, the collar's tenor and any unwind, roll, restrike or early termination must be more than three months apart, ruling out short-dated or frequently rolled structures.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The notification must confirm the Executive Team Member will be in compliance with the minimum shareholding policy after the trade, (if applicable).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The confirmer must be satisfied the Executive Team Member still meets the minimum shareholding after the collar, so the collared parcel must be sized to leave the minimum holding unhedged unless the Minimum Shareholding Policy says otherwise.

bespoke_clauses.topic: two week trading window in the notification
bespoke_clauses.clause: specify the proposed dates of the trade which should be no more than two weeks
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pricing, documentation and execution of the collar and the secured loan must all be completed inside the two-week window nominated in the notification, or a fresh notification and confirmation is needed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A clearance to trade can be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances; ... A decision to refuse clearance is final and binding ... the person seeking the clearance must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank cannot be told why a trade was blocked and confirmation can be withdrawn between pricing and settlement, so the trade documentation needs a condition precedent for subsisting clearance at execution.

bespoke_clauses.clause: IF YOU DO COME INTO POSSESSION OF INSIDE INFORMATION AFTER RECEIVING A CLEARANCE TO TRADE, YOU MUST NOT TRADE DESPITE HAVING RECEIVED THE CLEARANCE.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A cleared collar can become unexecutable at any point before signing, so the bank should expect a walk-away right on the executive's side.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A person is an “Associate” if a Director or co-worker is acting in concert with that person or if a Director or co-worker has, or can be regarded as having, investment control or influence over that person. Examples ... a trust of which the Director or co-worker ... are the trustee or beneficiary; ... a company which the Director or co-worker or their family controls.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking the collar or the loan through a family trust or controlled company does not avoid the consent, notification and Blackout Period requirements.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Following the end of each financial year, all Directors and Executive Team Members must certify to the Company Secretary that they and their Associates are in compliance with this policy (or advise of any breaches of this policy).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An outstanding collar and secured loan must remain compliant for its whole life and is re-attested annually, so a structure that drifts out of the minimum shareholding or is rolled inside three months surfaces at certification.

bespoke_clauses.clause: “Derivatives” includes warrants, exchange traded and over the counter options and contracts for differences.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no venue limitation, so an OTC put and call written with a bank is inside the derivatives regime rather than outside an exchange-limited ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: any other period that the Board specifies from time to time. If the Board specifies any other period, communications will be sent to you.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Additional blackouts are notified rather than kept confidential, so an executive can tell the bank a window is closed without breaching confidentiality, though the reason may not be disclosable.

summary: A funded collar is achievable under this policy, which is unusually permissive on the financing leg. Margin lending and other secured financing arrangements in respect of Amcor Securities are not prohibited but simply require the prior consent of the Company Secretary, and no criteria for that consent are stated, so the loan secured on the collared shares turns on a single internal approval. The put and call legs are Derivatives and Securities, so for Directors and Executive Team Members they require the clause 10 pre-trade notification to the Chairman of the Board or the CEO respectively, copied to the Company Secretary, with confirmation received before trading, execution within the nominated window of no more than two weeks, outside the 31 December and 30 June Blackout Periods and any Board-specified period, and with no inside information at signing. Hedging is absolutely prohibited over unvested plan securities, so only vested shares can be collared, and an Executive Team Member must confirm continued compliance with Amcor's Minimum Shareholding Policy after the trade, which caps the collared parcel. Tenor must exceed three months to avoid the short-term trading ban, and the structure benefits from Appendix 1 item 5, under which an involuntary disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights falls outside the policy altogether, so enforcement or a margin call sale during a Blackout Period is not a breach.
